content: 1. The implementation of pesticide legislation must be supported by the allocation of sufficient resources to ensure its effectiveness. 2. The management of public health pesticides is an underfunded and neglected area, requiring urgent attention and resource allocation. 3. Current activities by various international donors and agencies are fragmented and lack coordination, which is essential for an efficient and effective response. 4. The WHO Pesticide Evaluation Scheme (WHOPES) network consists of WHO Collaborating Centres, partner institutions, and field site locations, each with designated tasks and recent capacity-building efforts outlined by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation (BMGF) Project. 5. The International Pesticide Application Research Centre in Ascot, UK, has been testing insecticide application equipment globally since 1980. 6. The Laboratoire de Lutte Contre les Insectes Nuisibles in Montpellier, France, has been evaluating new public health pesticides globally since 1983, providing support in site assessment and training for new collaborating institutes. 7. The Vector Control Research Centre in Pondicherry, India, has been conducting research and training in lymphatic filariasis and integrated vector control methods, including insecticide efficacy testing, in Southeast Asia since 1985. Recent activities include preparing technical service agreements, assessing field sites, creating standard manuals, training staff, and facilitating exchange visits. 8. The Walloon Agricultural Research Centre in Gembloux, Belgium, has been involved in quality control of pesticides globally since 1998, supporting site assessments and training for new collaborating institutes. 9. The Insecticide and Insecticide Resistance Laboratory at the National Institute of Malaria Research in Delhi, India, has been conducting laboratory testing and evaluation of public health pesticides in Southeast Asia since 1999, with field sites in multiple Indian states. Activities include preparing technical service agreements, site assessments, equipment provision, standard manual preparation, staff training, and exchange visits. 10. The Department of Vector Biology and Control in Changping, China, has been engaged in vector surveillance and management since 2012. 11. The Institute of Tropical Medicine in Antwerp, Belgium, collaborates with institutions in Vietnam and Cambodia to conduct field studies on vector control products globally. Activities include preparing technical service agreements, assessing field sites, creating standard manuals, training staff, and facilitating exchange visits. 12. The London School of Hygiene and Tropical Medicine in the UK collaborates with institutions in Tanzania to conduct field studies on vector control products in East Africa. Activities include equipment provision, preparation of standard protocols, and exchange visits. 13. The Institut de Recherche pour le Développement in Cotonou, Benin, conducts field studies on vector control products in West Africa, providing equipment, preparing standard protocols, and facilitating exchange visits. 14. The Vector Control Research Unit in Penang, Malaysia, has been producing standard tools for laboratory studies on insecticide susceptibility globally. Activities include preparing technical service agreements, site assessments, quality control evaluations, equipment provision, standard manual preparation, staff training, and exchange visits. 15. The Noguchi Memorial Institute for Medical Research in Accra, Ghana, has been conducting field studies on vector control products in West Africa since 2009, with activities including exchange visits, equipment provision, and preparation of standard protocols. 16. The University of the Witwatersrand in Johannesburg, South Africa, conducted field studies on vector control products in South Africa from 2010 to 2012, focusing on equipment provision and preparation of standard protocols. 17. The Medical Research Council in Fajara, The Gambia, has been conducting field studies on vector control products in West Africa since 2011, with activities including staff training, equipment provision, standard protocol preparation, and exchange visits. 18. The Manatee County Mosquito Control in Palmetto, Florida, USA, has been conducting field studies on vector control products in the USA since 2011, focusing on the preparation of standard study protocols. 19. The Regional Medical Research Centre in Dibrugarh, Assam State, India, conducted field studies on vector control products in South Africa from 2011 to 2013, with activities including exchange visits, equipment provision, and preparation of standard protocols. 20. The Kenya Medical Research Institute in Nairobi, Kenya, has been conducting field studies on vector control products in West Africa since 2012, with activities including equipment provision, preparation of standard protocols, and exchange visits. 21. The Centre for Disease Control in Beijing, China, has been conducting field studies on vector control products in China since 2012, with activities including exchange visits, capacity assessments, preparation of technical service agreements, and standard protocol preparation. 22. The Instituto Nacional de Salud Publica in Tapachula, Mexico, has been conducting field studies on vector control products in Mexico and Central America since 2012, focusing on the preparation of standard protocols and provision of supplies. 23. The CDC in Atlanta, USA, has been conducting field studies on vector control products and quality control of pesticides globally since 2013.
